name: Exit this page
summary: Use Exit this page in sensitive services when viewing the page could put someone at risk and they may need to leave immediately.
whenToUse: Use only when sensitive page content could place a user in danger if another person sees it.
Use it as part of the complete GOV.UK pattern for leaving a page quickly, including the secondary hidden exit link and service-level safety decisions.
whenNotToUse: Do not use as a normal close, cancel, sign-out or back control.
Do not assume the component clears browser history, hides network activity or guarantees a user’s safety.

anatomy.name: Exit container
anatomy.description: The component module coordinates pointer, keyboard and repeated-key activation.

anatomy.name: Warning action
anatomy.description: A warning-styled link has button semantics and navigates to a safer neutral destination.

anatomy.name: Hidden emergency context
anatomy.description: Visually hidden text makes the urgency clear without lengthening the visible label.

anatomy.name: Secondary exit link
anatomy.description: The complete pattern includes an early hidden link to the same destination for assistive-technology users.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: A prominent emergency exit action near the top of a sensitive page.

behaviour: Initialise govuk-exit-this-page so the button supports the documented rapid keyboard gesture and enhanced loading feedback.
The ordinary href must navigate immediately when JavaScript is unavailable.
Choose a neutral, non-personalised destination and consider clearing sensitive application session data before redirecting.
accessibility: Position the action early in the page inside the width container and keep its focus treatment visible.
Provide the companion hidden exit link described by the full pattern, pointing to the same destination.
Test wording, placement and destination with people who face the relevant safety risk.
content: Keep the visible label direct, normally “Exit this page”.
Use visually hidden context such as “Emergency” where it makes the action clearer to screen-reader users.
Explain any limitations or additional safety advice elsewhere in the service without delaying the exit action.
